You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

candidate_edges.subject: Calciferol
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:

Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:

mineral oil (sometimes taken as a laxative).

These other drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

candidate_edges.subject: Calciferol
candidate_edges.object: dose needs may be different during pregnancy
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

candidate_edges.subject: ondansetron (oral)
candidate_edges.object: many other drugs can interact with ondansetron
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

Use: -Prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting
Usual Adult Dose for Nausea/Vomiting--Radiation Induced:
The recommended dose is 8 mg orally 3 times a day.
For total body irradiation, the dose is 8 mg orally 1 to 2 hours before each fraction of radiotherapy administered each day.

For single high-dose fraction radiotherapy to the abdomen, subsequent doses are 8 mg orally every 8 hours after the first dose.

congestive heart failure, slow heartbeats;
a personal or family history of long QT syndrome; or
a blockage in your digestive tract (stomach or intestines).

Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

Follow your doctor's dosing instructions very carefully.
Take the ondansetron regular tablet with a full glass of water.
To take the orally disintegrating tablet (Zofran ODT):
Keep the tablet in its blister pack until you are ready to take it.
Open the package and peel back the foil.
Do not push a tablet through the foil or you may damage the tablet.
Use dry hands to remove the tablet and place it in your mouth.
Do not swallow the tablet whole.
Allow it to dissolve in your mouth without chewing.
Swallow several times as the tablet dissolves.
To use ondansetron oral soluble film (strip) (Zuplenz):

candidate_edges.object: many other drugs can interact with ondansetron
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

Cyclobenzaprine is a prescription muscle relaxant.
It is used short-term to relieve muscle spasms.
The spasms are caused by sprains, strains, and injuries.
These include low back and neck pain.
It is used together with rest and physical therapy.
This combination helps relieve pain, tenderness, and limited movement.
These symptoms are caused by muscle spasm.
1,2
Cyclobenzaprine is used to treat fibromyalgia in adults.
It can help reduce pain.
For fibromyalgia, it is taken as a sublingual (under the tongue) tablet at bedtime under the brand name Tonmya.
In clinical trials, Tonmya significantly reduced fibromyalgia pain compared with placebo over 14 weeks.
Close to half of treated patients achieved at least a 30% improvement in pain.
3
The Flexeril brand has been discontinued.
Cyclobenzaprine is available as generic tablets.
Cyclobenzaprine is also available as the brand-name products Amrix and Fexmid.

:
Yes, drowsiness is the most common side effect of the tablets.
This side effect affects up to 38% of people taking the 10 mg dose.
These figures are from clinical trials.
This is one reason 5 mg is the usual starting dose.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.
1,2

Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.

Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.

This combination helps relieve pain, tenderness, and limited movement.

Cyclobenzaprine is also available as the brand-name products Amrix and Fexmid.

Cyclobenzaprine dose for muscle spasm:
Cyclobenzaprine is usually taken for up to 2 or 3 weeks for muscle spasm.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Immediate-release tablets are taken three times a day.
Extended-release capsules are taken once daily, at about the same time each day.
Swallow the capsules whole.
You can open the capsule if you have difficulty swallowing them.
Sprinkle the contents onto a tablespoon of applesauce.
Swallow the mixture right away.
Do not chew the mixture.
Follow your doctor's dosing instructions very carefully.
Cyclobenzaprine for fibromyalgia:
Tonmya is taken once daily at bedtime, after brushing your teeth.
Drink a few sips of water first so your mouth is moist.
Place the tablet(s) under your tongue until dissolved.
Do not swallow whole, cut, crush, or chew.
Avoid eating or drinking for at least 15 minutes afterward.
Avoid hot, cold, or acidic drinks until morning.
Avoid talking for about 5 minutes after dosing.

Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.

The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.

Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.

graph_edge.relation_definition: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
graph_edge.evidence_text:
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have congestive heart failure.
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have a heart rhythm or conduction problem including heart block.
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have recently had a heart attack.
Do not take cyclobenzaprine within 14 days of taking an MAO inhibitor.
1,2,3
MAO inhibitors.
Do not take MAO inhibitors with cyclobenzaprine.
These MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, and tranylcypromine.
Dangerously high fever, seizures, and deaths have occurred when cyclobenzaprine or similar drugs were combined with these medicines.
1,2,3
Serotonin syndrome.
Cyclobenzaprine can cause a serious condition called serotonin syndrome.
This condition occurs when cyclobenzaprine is taken with certain other medicines.
These medicines include antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics), tramadol, bupropion, meperidine, and verapamil.
Get medical help right away if you have agitation.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have congestive heart failure.
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have a heart rhythm or conduction problem including heart block.
Do not take cyclobenzaprine if you have recently had a heart attack.
Do not take cyclobenzaprine within 14 days of taking an MAO inhibitor.
1,2,3
MAO inhibitors.
Do not take MAO inhibitors with cyclobenzaprine.
These MAO inhibitors include isocarboxazid, linezolid, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, and tranylcypromine.
Dangerously high fever, seizures, and deaths have occurred when cyclobenzaprine or similar drugs were combined with these medicines.
1,2,3
Serotonin syndrome.
Cyclobenzaprine can cause a serious condition called serotonin syndrome.
This condition occurs when cyclobenzaprine is taken with certain other medicines.
These medicines include antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics), tramadol, bupropion, meperidine, and verapamil.
Get medical help right away if you have agitation.

candidate_edges.subject: Cyclobenzaprine
candidate_edges.relation_definition: The subject drug is used together with the other treatment or lifestyle measure specified by the object entity.
candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine is a prescription muscle relaxant.
It is used short-term to relieve muscle spasms.
The spasms are caused by sprains, strains, and injuries.
These include low back and neck pain.
It is used together with rest and physical therapy.
This combination helps relieve pain, tenderness, and limited movement.
These symptoms are caused by muscle spasm.
1,2
Cyclobenzaprine is used to treat fibromyalgia in adults.
It can help reduce pain.
For fibromyalgia, it is taken as a sublingual (under the tongue) tablet at bedtime under the brand name Tonmya.
In clinical trials, Tonmya significantly reduced fibromyalgia pain compared with placebo over 14 weeks.
Close to half of treated patients achieved at least a 30% improvement in pain.
3
The Flexeril brand has been discontinued.
Cyclobenzaprine is available as generic tablets.
Cyclobenzaprine is also available as the brand-name products Amrix and Fexmid.
2,4

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine dose for muscle spasm:
Cyclobenzaprine is usually taken for up to 2 or 3 weeks for muscle spasm.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Immediate-release tablets are taken three times a day.
Extended-release capsules are taken once daily, at about the same time each day.
Swallow the capsules whole.
You can open the capsule if you have difficulty swallowing them.
Sprinkle the contents onto a tablespoon of applesauce.
Swallow the mixture right away.
Do not chew the mixture.
Follow your doctor's dosing instructions very carefully.
Cyclobenzaprine for fibromyalgia:
Tonmya is taken once daily at bedtime, after brushing your teeth.
Drink a few sips of water first so your mouth is moist.
Place the tablet(s) under your tongue until dissolved.
Do not swallow whole, cut, crush, or chew.
Avoid eating or drinking for at least 15 minutes afterward.
Avoid hot, cold, or acidic drinks until morning.
Avoid talking for about 5 minutes after dosing.

Cyclobenzaprine is usually taken for up to 2 or 3 weeks for muscle spasm.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Immediate-release tablets are taken three times a day.
Extended-release capsules are taken once daily, at about the same time each day.
Swallow the capsules whole.
You can open the capsule if you have difficulty swallowing them.
Sprinkle the contents onto a tablespoon of applesauce.
Swallow the mixture right away.
Do not chew the mixture.
Follow your doctor's dosing instructions very carefully.
Cyclobenzaprine for fibromyalgia:
Tonmya is taken once daily at bedtime, after brushing your teeth.
Drink a few sips of water first so your mouth is moist.
Place the tablet(s) under your tongue until dissolved.
Do not swallow whole, cut, crush, or chew.
Avoid eating or drinking for at least 15 minutes afterward.
Avoid hot, cold, or acidic drinks until morning.
Avoid talking for about 5 minutes after dosing.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.
The relationship also explains some of its most important drug interactions.
1,2

Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Therefore, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of such diseases include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.

Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.

This relationship explains several of its side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.

Unlike most water pills, spironolactone makes your body keep potassium in.
Most water pills make you lose potassium.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Why is spironolactone described as a high-risk medicine?
:
The main reason is the risk of a high potassium level.
A high potassium level can cause a dangerous change in your heart rhythm.
A high potassium level often gives no warning symptoms.
The risk rises if your kidneys do not work well.
The risk rises if you take other medicines that raise potassium.
Several very common medicines raise potassium.
Ibuprofen is a very common medicine that raises potassium.
Some blood pressure tablets are very common medicines that raise potassium.
This risk is manageable.
Blood tests are built into treatment.
Your potassium should be checked within a week of starting spironolactone or changing your dose.
It should be checked regularly after that.
Spironolactone also needs care in pregnancy and in people with liver disease.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
The most important interactions with spironolactone are medicines that also raise potassium.
The combined effect of these medicines can push your potassium level dangerously high.
Tell your doctor about every medicine you take, including anything you start or stop during treatment.
Be especially careful with:
eplerenone, which should not be taken with spironolactone at all;
medicines that raise potassium, including ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril and ramipril, ARBs such as losartan and valsartan, NSAIDs, heparin and low molecular weight heparin, and trimethoprim;
potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes, which are usually stopped when spironolactone is started for heart failure;
Spironolactone slows how fast your kidneys clear lithium.
Spironolactone can cause lithium toxicity.
Lithium levels need monitoring.
Digoxin needs care for two separate reasons.
Spironolactone interferes with one type of blood test used to measure digoxin.
Spironolactone can raise the actual amount of digoxin in your body.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Take spironolactone exactly as prescribed.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides.
Take it the same way each day, either always with food or always without.
Food increases how much spironolactone your body absorbs.
This increase roughly doubles the amount absorbed.
Switching back and forth changes how much medicine you actually get.
Shake the oral liquid well before every dose.
Measure it with the marked oral syringe, dosing spoon, or medicine cup that comes with it.
Do not use a kitchen spoon.
Do not switch between tablets and the oral liquid without your doctor changing the dose.
They are not interchangeable.
The liquid gives a higher level of medicine in your blood for the same number of milligrams.
You will need regular blood tests to check your potassium, sodium, kidney function, uric acid, and blood sugar.
Keep these appointments even if you feel completely well.
If you are being treated for high blood pressure, keep taking spironolactone even when you feel fine.
High blood pressure usually has no symptoms.

candidate_edges.evidence_text:
Is spironolactone a diuretic?
:
Yes.
Spironolactone is a diuretic, or water pill.
It belongs to the group called potassium-sparing diuretics.
It works by blocking aldosterone, a hormone that makes your kidneys hold onto salt and water.
Unlike most water pills, spironolactone makes your body keep potassium in.
Most water pills make you lose potassium.
It is a weaker diuretic than medicines such as furosemide.
Furosemide is one reason it is often given alongside another water pill.
It is often given alongside another water pill rather than instead of one.
Is spironolactone used for acne?
:
Spironolactone is not approved by the FDA for treating acne.
Doctors sometimes prescribe it off-label for hormonal acne in women.
Off-label means a doctor is prescribing a medicine for something other than its approved uses.
Off-label prescribing is legal.
Off-label prescribing is common.
Off-label prescribing means the FDA has not reviewed the medicine for that purpose.
The reason it is used this way relates to how spironolactone works.
Spironolactone blocks aldosterone.

This is a decision to make with your doctor rather than by stopping on your own.
Breastfeeding:
Spironolactone itself does not pass into breast milk.
Its active breakdown product is canrenone.
Canrenone has been found in breast milk.
It is found in very small amounts.
These amounts are not expected to affect a breastfed baby.
No side effects were reported in the one infant studied over a short period.
The long-term picture is not known.
Talk to your doctor so you can weigh this up together.
Children:
Spironolactone has not been shown to be safe and effective in children.
The oral liquid is specifically not recommended for treating high blood pressure in children.
This is because of the hormonal effects of the medicine.
Any use in a child must be decided and monitored by a specialist.
Older adults:
Spironolactone is cleared by the kidneys.
Kidney function tends to fall with age.

Why is spironolactone described as a high-risk medicine?
:
The main reason is the risk of a high potassium level.
A high potassium level can cause a dangerous change in your heart rhythm.
A high potassium level often gives no warning symptoms.
The risk rises if your kidneys do not work well.
The risk rises if you take other medicines that raise potassium.
Several very common medicines raise potassium.
Ibuprofen is a very common medicine that raises potassium.
Some blood pressure tablets are very common medicines that raise potassium.
This risk is manageable.
Blood tests are built into treatment.
Your potassium should be checked within a week of starting spironolactone or changing your dose.
It should be checked regularly after that.
Spironolactone also needs care in pregnancy and in people with liver disease.
